samples.summary: The safety-critical ordering in `api-keys create` (validate --format BEFORE minting the key) has no test
samples.evidence: api-keys.ts:21-27 moves `parseOutputFormat(opts.format)` above `createApiKey(name)` with a comment stating the whole point: "a bad `--format` must not discard a raw key that the server will never show again." No test exercises this. status.test.ts's wiring suite only registers status/ctx/schema (status.test.ts:130-132); namespaces.test.ts only asserts command names/aliases; grep for `createApiKey`/`registerApiKeysCommand` across packages/cli/test finds no invocation of the action handler. A regression that moved the parse back below the API call (re-introducing the key-loss bug) would keep the suite green, since parseOutputFormat itself is tested only in isolation (output.test.ts:56-72).

samples.summary: parseOutputFormat added to ~20 command call sites (docs, notes, slides, cells, tabs, sheets-import); none are covered by a wiring test
samples.evidence: The diff wires `parseOutputFormat` into docs.ts, notes.ts, slides.ts, cells.ts, tabs.ts, sheets-import.ts, but the only end-to-end `--format bogus` assertions are for status, ctx list and schema (status.test.ts:168-185, 230-234). Dropping the call from any of the other files would not fail any test. Sheets-import is the riskiest: it aliases the parsed value to `outFmt` alongside a separate file-format `fmt` (sheets-import.ts:50-51), an easy variable mix-up nothing would catch.

samples.summary: `expect(table).not.toContain('[object Object]')` in the status table test is vacuous — the status payload has no nested values
samples.evidence: status.test.ts:81-87 is presented as proof that the new `cell()` JSON-serialization in table.ts fixes `[object Object]`, but buildStatus returns only scalars/null (status.ts buildStatus), so `String()` would never have produced `[object Object]` for it. The assertion passes with or without the table.ts change. The claim 'renders every field' is also unverified: `toContain('hackerwins')` is satisfied by the email alone, and fields such as workspaceId/expiresAt/loggedIn are never asserted.

samples.summary: The array branch of formatTable still uses raw String() for cells; no test covers a nested object inside an array row
samples.evidence: table.ts:53 renders array rows with `String(row[k] ?? '')`, bypassing the new `cell()` helper that JSON-serializes objects (table.ts:7-10). Tests only exercise nested values through the single-object path (status.test.ts:236-241 uses `schema ctx.list`, a record) — output.test.ts's array table test (lines 20-32) uses flat strings. So the '[object Object]' behavior for list-returning commands (e.g. docs list with nested fields) is both unfixed and untested.

samples.summary: 'is JSON-parseable as emitted by the default format' asserts a JSON round-trip, which holds for any plain object
samples.evidence: ctx.test.ts:44-47 asserts `JSON.parse(format(rows,'json'))` equals `rows` — true for any JSON-serializable value regardless of buildWorkspaceList's behavior or the format plumbing. The analogous status.test.ts:74-79 test only re-asserts `loggedIn`, already covered by lines 40-58. Neither can fail if the feature under change breaks.

samples.summary: `status --format csv` test asserts only the header line, not the value row
samples.evidence: status.test.ts:163-166 checks `lastStdout().split('\n')[0] === 'loggedIn,message'`; the data row (`false,"Not logged in..."`) is never asserted, so a CSV value-encoding regression (e.g. quoting of the message containing a comma-free but backticked string) would go unnoticed. Similarly `workspaceName: null` rendering through `cell()` (empty string) is untested in any table test.

verdict.reason: Verified independently: api-keys.ts:20-27 places parseOutputFormat before createApiKey with an explicit safety rationale, but no test anywhere exercises the `api-keys create` action. Repo-wide grep for api-keys|createApiKey|registerApiKeysCommand yields only structural assertions (namespaces.test.ts:27-54 asserts command name/alias; schema.test.ts:32-34,54,82-85 asserts schema registry entries) - neither invokes an action handler. The only suite that actually parses a commander program (status.test.ts:128-134) registers status/ctx/schema only, and its `--format bogus` cases (lines 168-173, 181-185, 230-234) never touch api-keys. output.test.ts:56-72 tests parseOutputFormat in isolation and would pass regardless of call ordering. Backend api-key-http.e2e-spec.ts is HTTP-only (no spawn/execFile/runCli matches), and the CLI-roundtrip e2e specs only exercise docs/notes content --format. vitest.config.ts:5 limits CLI test discovery to test/**/*.test.ts, bounding the search space, and no lint or static rule enforces the ordering. A regression moving the parse below the minting call would keep the suite green - a real, unmitigated missing-test gap for a safety-relevant behavior, major under the test-adequacy rubric.
